title: Write the script templates of an issuer response

blocks.text: Your issuer has started sending scripts to unblock PINs and block lost cards' applications. In the test lab some terminals answer every response that carries a script with "chip data format error", and the scripts never run.

`IssuerResponse.de55` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/IssuerResponse.java` writes the response's DE 55 byte by byte, without `TLVList`, as the network's reference implementation does. Tag `91` already goes out. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `length`: the bytes that announce a value's length;
`template`: one script, ready for the card.

blocks.text: The scripts come in every size the network allows, with or without an identifier. About twelve lines in total.

cases.says: tag 91 comes first, then each script with its identifier and commands in the order given, and nothing at all when there is nothing to send
a template's length counts its encoded elements, tags and lengths included, so the template parses as a TLV list
a value of 128 bytes or more is announced with 81 or 82 and the length, for commands and templates alike
the script identifier is optional, and a script without one has no 9F18 element, not an empty one

origin.section: 18.5. The Response Carries the ARPC in Tag 91 and the Scripts as TLV Inside TLV

concepts: The response's DE 55 carries tag 91 and script templates 71 and 72, each a constructed TLV of an optional 9F18 and 86 commands, whose length counts the encoded elements.
